entities.name: Anselm of Besate
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Anselm of Besate was an influential 11th-century churchman and rhetorician from the medieval Christian world.

Born around 1010 in Besate, a town in the County of Besate, within the Kingdom of Croatia (part of the Holy Roman Empire), he went on to become a prominent figure in the Catholic Church.

Anselm's most notable achievement was his role in shaping the theological and liturgical practices of the medieval Church, particularly through his work on the 'Investitures Controversy,' which led to the establishment of the Investiture Controversy of 1075.

He was also a key figure in the development of Scholasticism, influencing prominent thinkers such as Thomas Aquinas.

Anselm's legacy extends beyond his own time, with his ideas and writings continuing to shape Christian theology and spirituality for centuries to come.

A testament to his enduring impact is the numerous churches and monasteries he helped establish during his lifetime, many of which remain standing today, a lasting cultural footprint that underscores his significance in the arc of world history.
